note: Painted and bare ironwork with bronze fittings, dry. Colours are sRGB 0-255. First used on the Frastown West Berth kit, whose art direction names plate steel, old teal and oxide.

tread_plate.use: A plate that is walked and driven on. Raised-lozenge tread; wheel lines and a foundry die come from the recipe.

plain_plate.use: Smooth rolled plate that is walked on: bridge treads, hatch leaves, thresholds.

palm_rail.use: A rail or rung a hand rests on. Browned iron, burnished along the crown where it is held.

worn_iron.use: Unpainted iron fittings: strakes, flanges, grate bars, collars, rivet heads.

bronze.use: Bronze fittings. Tarnish on the faces, verdigris in the creases, bright on the edges.

old_teal_paint.use: Paint over red-oxide primer over iron, on plates and webs.

plate_steel_paint.use: The same paint system in slate, a little more worn, on structural sections.
